newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bishop Belo meets Kohl for delayed Indonesia talks.
newsitem.headline: Bishop Belo meets Kohl for delayed Indonesia talks.

text.p: Carlos Belo, the Roman Catholic Bishop who won the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize, received support from German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Monday for his efforts to secure peace in his homeland of East Timor.
After a meeting in Bonn, Kohl praised Belo for his "level-headed and non-violent work for his flock and the people of East Timor", government spokesman Peter Hausmann said in a statement.

Kohl, who tried in vain to meet Belo on a trip to Indonesia in October, stressed the importance of a peaceful and just settlement for East Timor involving respect for its human rights and cultural identity.

East Timor, with a population of more than 800,000 people, was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and annexed by Jakarta a year later in an act not recognised by the United Nations, which still regards Portugal as the territory's administering power.
Belo has kept an extremely low profile during his visit to Germany. He was filmed at one mass but has made few comments to reporters.
Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel also met Belo on Monday.
"Human rights have to be respected and living conditions have to be improved for the people in East Timor," Kinkel said in a statement.
Belo told reporters on Sunday he did not want to be viewed as a politician but would continue working hard for peace in East Timor.
He said political questions should be addressed to the co-winner of the Nobel prize, East Timorese-born activist Jose Ramos Horta, who lives in self-imposed exile in Australia.
Ramos Horta has accused Jakarta of pressuring Belo not to use this week's awards ceremony in Oslo to attack Indonesia.
Belo had planned to meet Kohl during his visit to Indonesia in October but the meeting collapsed when Belo said he had not been officially invited and had pastoral duties to fulfil.
